html:
Muhammad Ali was an American boxer, three times world heavyweight champion, and one of the most famous people of the 20th century.

Born Cassius Clay in Louisville, Kentucky, he won Olympic gold in Rome in 1960. In 1964 he beat Sonny Liston for the world title. Soon after, he joined the Nation of Islam, where Malcolm X was then his friend, and took the name Muhammad Ali.

In 1967 he refused to be drafted to fight in the Vietnam War. He was stripped of his title, banned from boxing for over three years, and convicted. The Supreme Court overturned the conviction in 1971. His stand made him a hero to many Black Americans and to the anti war movement.

  • 1971: lost the "Fight of the Century" to Joe Frazier.
  • 1974: took back the title from George Foreman in the Rumble in the Jungle in Kinshasa, Zaire.
  • 1975: beat Frazier in the "Thrilla in Manila".

He was fast, witty and loud ("float like a butterfly, sting like a bee"). He later had Parkinson's disease, and lit the Olympic flame in Atlanta in 1996.
sum: Muhammad Ali was an American boxer, three times world heavyweight champion, and one of the most famous people of the 20th century.
